widgets_values:
# CustomCharacterCreator V.4 (Simple) — End User Guide

## Overview

CustomCharacterCreator V.4 (Simple) is a ComfyUI workflow that builds a **multi-view character dataset** from a single reference image. It generates a set of **named scene "passes"** (e.g. `T-POSE`, `CLOSE-FRONT`, `OFFICE`, `RUNNING`, `COFFEE`…) and saves them straight into the dataset.

This is the **Simple variant** — it has **no Upscaler and no Face Detailer**. If you need those optional post-processing stages, use the **ADV** version of this workflow.

Dataset tagging lives in a **separate standalone tagging workflow**, which keeps this graph focused on generation.

### Color legend (how to read the canvas)

| Zone color | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Grey** | Model loaders, settings, and output/naming |
| **Green** | Your inputs (reference image, style/clothes prompts) |
| **Purple** | The scene passes — one group per shot |

---

## Required Custom Nodes

Install these packs before using the workflow — the graph depends on them.

| Node Pack | Used for |
|-----------|----------|
| **ComfyUI-KJNodes** | Core routing (`GetNode`/`SetNode`), `JoinStringMulti`, `ImageResizeKJv2`, `StringConstantMultiline`. |
| **ComfyUI-Easy-Use** | `easy ifElse` and float inputs. |
| **ComfyUI-Flux2Klein-Enhancer** | `IdentityGuidance` for the Flux Klein chain. |
| **ComfyUI Impact Pack** | The Save-Dataset switch (`ImpactInversedSwitch`). |
| **ComfyUI-AutoCropFaces** | Reference-face detection / crop preparation. |
| **WAS Node Suite** | `Image Save` — the final dataset export. |
| **Mickmumpitz-Nodes** | `ImageCollect`, `ImageCollectUnpack`, and the labels. |

The per-scene generation subgraphs are **built-in ComfyUI** — no extra pack needed.

---

## Required Models

| Model file | Loader | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| **flux2-vae.safetensors** | VAE Loader | VAE for the main image chain. |
| **qwen_3_8b_fp8mixed.safetensors** | CLIP Loader (type `flux2`) | Text/instruction encoder. |
| **flux-2-klein-9b-fp8.safetensors** | UNET Loader | Main generation model. |
| **Flux2-Klein-9B-consistency-V2.safetensors** | LoRA (strength **0.35**) | Consistency LoRA — keep enabled. |

---

## 1. Load the Models

In the grey **model-loader** zone, load the four generation models above (VAE, CLIP, UNET, LoRA). The LoRA strength is set to **0.35** by default.

---

## 2. Output Naming  (the grey "OUTPUT NAMING" zone)

Naming is **fully automatic and relative** — you set one main field and everything files itself under `ComfyUI/output/`.

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **NAME (CHARACTER)** | `MyCharacter` | The one field you change per run — the character/run name. |
| **ROOT FOLDER** | `CCC` | Top-level bucket for all your datasets. |
| **TYPE** | `IMG_GEN` / `DATASET` | Stage labels (leave as-is). |

These compose into a tidy tree:

```
ComfyUI/output/
  CCC/
    MyCharacter/
      MyCharacter_IMG_GEN/     ← raw per-scene generations
      MyCharacter_DATASET/     ← final dataset export
```

- **Nothing is hardcoded to your machine** — the workflow runs on any PC unchanged.
- **Folders are created automatically** — you do *not* need to pre-make them.
- For a clean run per character, just change **NAME**. Change **ROOT FOLDER** to start a new project bucket.
- Advanced: the final export uses a WAS `Image Save` node — a power user can still type an **absolute path** into its location field to export straight into a training folder.

### Resolution

Resolution is set with the **Resolution Selector** — pick an **aspect ratio** (default `1:1 (Square)`) and a size multiplier.

---

## 3. User Input  (the green "Inputs" zone)

1. Load your **reference image** (the character to recreate).
2. Fill in the two prompt fields:
   - **Style Prompt** — overall visual style / aesthetic.
   - **Clothes Prompt** — outfit details.

---

## 4. Dataset Creation  (the purple scene groups)

Each **purple group is one scene pass** with a short name matching its prompt (`T-POSE`, `CLOSE-ANGRY`, `OFFICE`, `COFFEE`, `FLYING`…). Each group is self-contained. You can:

- **edit** the prompt in a group,
- **duplicate** a group (copy/paste) to add more scenes,
- **disable** a group (mute it) to generate fewer images,
- **rename** the group to match its new prompt.

Prompts are assembled with `JoinStringMulti`, so you decide per group whether the **Style** and **Clothes** prompts apply — just keep or disconnect `Get_style` / `Get_clothes` from that group's join chain.

You can also point a group at a **different source image** via its `Get INPUT IMAGE`, to remix source references instead of always using the main one.

**Important:** any image you want in the final dataset must be added by wiring its `ImageCollect` node into the shared `Dataset`.

> Prompt conventions used here: describe **the character** (never state a gender), and avoid camera/film-look styling (no "shot on iPhone", "grainy", "flash photography", etc.) so the dataset stays consistent.

---

## Separate Tagging Workflow

If you need captions, use the dedicated tagging workflow — robust QwenVL-based LLM tagging, compatible with JSON tags for Ideogram 4.

---

## Recommended Order

1. Load the four models.
2. Set **NAME (CHARACTER)** (and **ROOT FOLDER** if starting a new project).
3. Pick the **aspect ratio** in the Resolution Selector.
4. Load the **reference image** and write the **Style** / **Clothes** prompts.
5. Run — each enabled scene is generated and saved to the dataset.

Change **NAME** for each character/run — every stage refiles automatically under `output/CCC/<NAME>/`, so there is no folder to pre-create and nothing to clean up between runs.
